blocks.text: That matter remained in the mind of the English general. When he came to Ludhiana and met the Singhs, he asked again about their origin. (9)
The general reflected that the emperor’s written account could not be accepted without scrutiny.
He summoned Captain Murray, who knew many people of the region, and told him to have the origin of the Singhs written down — how the Khalsa attained sovereignty. (10–11)
He also said that the emperor’s version could not be the whole truth, for Hindus and Muslims had long stood in enmity and no Muslim historian could be trusted blindly here. (12–13)
